A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model FID/CLIP evaluations, ImageNet and CIFAR-10 classification results, scale-learning comparisons, and CPU runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds calibration-based training comparisons and evaluation on MJHQ.

M1.justification: The group-wise quantization procedure, shared noise-trained Winograd scales, objectives, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The added calibration modes are comparison variants, and Section 13 documents the previously reported optimized kernels. Appendix matrix corrections do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: v2 adds DiffusionDB prompts for training calibration-based comparators and MJHQ for text-to-image transfer evaluation. COCO, ImageNet, CIFAR-10, and the existing task coverage are retained; the additions extend the existing image-generation task.

E2.justification: New Table 8 evaluates end-to-end calibration-based scale learning, calibration-based transformation-matrix learning, and BRECQ-style scale learning against noise-trained scales. Existing BQW, PAW+FSQ, Q-Diffusion, and noise-trained transformation comparisons remain. The new discussion of BQW and PAW+FSQ does not establish additional diffusion-model evaluations of those methods.

E3.justification: Section 9 introduces protocols using 10,000 randomly selected calibration prompts, image/feature reconstruction losses, and end-to-end or BRECQ training, including layer-specific scales for BRECQ. The new MJHQ-2k evaluation specifies 25 DPMSolver++ steps and guidance 5.0. Previously stated evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of the central data-free rationale: Table 8 directly compares noise-based learning with calibration-based end-to-end and BRECQ alternatives. Table 12 extends scale-transfer testing from the retained CIFAR-10 analysis to diffusion generation on MJHQ. These add substantive methodological and transfer analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, performance error bars, or significance tests. Figure 3's retained standard deviations describe activation distributions, not uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and 7 revise numerous Winograd scores under unchanged stated COCO settings. For example, learned-scale InstaFlow F(6,3) with TEASD changes from FID/CLIP 34.00/28.93 to 27.69/29.46, while F(4,3) with AKL changes from 23.38/30.07 to 24.51/29.87. Tables 8 and 12 add calibration and MJHQ results, and Figures 4–5 update restored-image examples. Classification, Q-Diffusion, and inference-runtime results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix Section 7.1 corrects several F(6,3) matrix signs: Equation 30 changes the sixth-row, third-column entry of A-transpose from 1 to -1; Equation 32 corrects three entries in G's third column. The general mathematical formulation and derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about data-free fully quantized Winograd convolution, near-full-precision quality, generalization, and runtime benefits. The stated 31.3% convolution speedup and 1.62/2.56 percentage-point classification advantages are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 9 adds interpretations of calibration's weaker F(6,3) results, possible sample-size and overfitting effects, and BRECQ's greater training cost. Section 13 explains kernel efficiency and argues applicability to other processor architectures. These extend the discussion without changing the existing FID caveat or broad generalization claims.

D1.justification: New Section 13 substantially expands implementation documentation through operand reuse, SIMD reduction handling, offline weight repacking, and matrix-multiply instruction details. It also supplies a previously absent code-access link. Section 9 adds calibration-training resource information. These document existing kernels and new comparison experiments; repository contents were not accessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DiffusionDB reference and expands positioning against already cited BRECQ, BQW, and PAW+FSQ, discussing calibration requirements and which Winograd operations they quantize. The main related-work account and other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 inserts supplementary Sections 9 and 13, expands the transferability discussion, and renumbers subsequent appendix sections. Most existing prose, including the main narrative, remains verbatim; there is no extensive rewrite or reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8 and 12, moves table captions above the tables, and corrects the Q-Diffusion table captions' reference to Winograd convolution. Figure 3 is redrawn at higher resolution with the same data, and Figures 4–5 are refreshed. Figures 7–12 retain identical image grids despite pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The calibration comparisons and MJHQ transfer test strengthen support for the data-free approach, while corrected matrix signs and new kernel/code-access documentation improve accuracy and reproducibility. These provide a bounded overall gain. The main-table score revisions remain unexplained, and the added tests still do not establish the paper's broad guarantee of generalization.
